entities.text: Devineni Bhramanda Rao vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short 'Cr.P.C.') by the petitioner, who is arrayed as accused No.18, seeking to quash the proceedings against him in Crime No.1017 of 2023 on the file of Raidurgam, Cyberabad District, Rangareddy District, registered for the alleged offences punishable under Sections 409, 477, 420, 423, 120b read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 156(3) of Criminal Procedure Code.

2. Heard Sri J.C.Francis, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Ganesh, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for respondent No.1 - State.
3.
As seen from the record, the averments of the petition do not constitute offences under Section 409 of IPC.

Hence, this Court deems it appropriate to direct the petitioner to appear before the Investigating Officer on or before 26.06.2024 between 11:00 a.m. and 05:00 p.m. and in turn, the Investigating Officer is directed to follow the procedure laid down under Section 41-A Cr.P.C. and also the guidelines formulated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar 1 scrupulously.

entities.text: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the petitioner shall co-operate with the Investigating Officer as and when required by furnishing information and the petitioner shall submit his defense and produce all relevant documents/material required for the purpose of the investigation and the Investigating Officer shall consider the same before filing appropriate report before the learned Magistrate concerned.
4. Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is disposed of.
Miscellaneous applications, if any pending, shall also stand closed.
